recipe.notes: CPU evidence (research lane r-zerank2): the derived template renders byte-identically through transformers' own apply_chat_template and a hand-rolled environment, token ids match the paper's render with add_special_tokens True==False, truncation at 8192 is identical, the prompt ends with the assistant header, and the paper's strip is the family's declared normalisation (below) (10 PASS, 0 failures; the mutation re-gating the generation prompt fails). This recipe declares that template and adds the `messages is defined` guard so the harness's stage-1 template check (which renders the file from the plain request texts) and the engine's score route (which renders it over query/document messages) execute different branches that produce the same prompt: stage 1 asserts the plain-text branch against the declared shape (template_render_check, zero tolerance), the recipe's tests additionally render the engine's messages context with the serving environment's jinja settings and assert byte-identity with it and with the declared shape's render for every sampled row, and stage 2 on the GPU wave exercises the engine branch end to end. The paper's query.strip()/doc.strip() is the declared content normalisation (client.template normalize: [strip]): fit strips the spans before measuring, the wire ships the stripped spans and the reference's spans agree byte for byte on every under-cap row (the r-zerank2 "strip asymmetry" closes as declared policy, one rule for the family). Known served-vs-reference differences, all inherited from the paper's served path and recorded in the research report section 6: (1) the reference truncates only the whole rendered prompt at 8192 (declared known_deviations: anchor_drop_over_cap), the served path cuts the content spans and keeps the anchor; (2) the settle rule (above) settles a query over its 4096-token share served-side while the in-process reference keeps it whole (experiments/paper/rerankers/zerank_2.yaml); over-share queries are declared divergence rows - an over-share query in an UNDER-budget pair is an under-cap row and gates red by design (the reference never ports the client's settle rule), so the wave's pairs files keep queries well within the share and drop any row stage 1 goes red on; (3) the score-head matmul runs in fp32 on the engine (head_dtype default for pooling) and bf16 in the reference - expected well inside the probability gates; (4) reference.py's --mode render writes the paper's own cut as the content spans (the whole-prompt right cut at raw character offsets; under the cap the stripped texts), never the client's cut. template.jinja is the family's file name (formerly zerank2_score_template.jinja). GPU wave must also: run the negative control (serve without --chat-template falls back to raw concatenation with no warning on this model), and check /tokenize agreement (stage 1 does with an engine URL).
